Anya (eng-runtime): Heads-up — running the function-calling + JSON-mode replay harness this morning and seeing a measurable perf hit vs text-mode. p50 +12%, p95 +23% on the same model/config. :eyes:
Sam (bench): ugh. can you paste the exact command + config you used?
Anya (eng-runtime): ran:```./bench_replay --mode=json --clients=200 --duration=300 --kernel=auto --batching=dynamic --batch-window-ms=20 --kv_cache=enabled --validate_json=true --replay-file=prod_sample_2026-03-15.pbz```
Raj (perf): do we know if kernel selection diverged between runs? `--kernel=auto` can pick different kernels based on token shapes. sometimes json-mode increases token length because of schema fields which flips the kernel.
Kai (infra): PerfBot posted a run summary: https://perf.redwood/summary/1769876543 (bot)
PerfBot: benchmark run uploaded: run_id=run_1769876543, mode=json, clients=200, batching=dynamic, kernels=auto, kv_cache=on, validate_json=on, notes="replay harness with original client timings"
Sam (bench): quick diff vs text-run: text-run (same replay file, kernel=auto) -> p95 142ms, json-run -> p95 175ms. token counts roughly +8% in json-mode because of function meta.
Raj (perf): seeing two possible culprits: 1) kernel selection changed -> slower attention kernels; 2) KV cache hit rate dropped because serialized JSON changes prefixes so fewer cache hits.
Anya (eng-runtime): I profiled a small sample. flame snippet:```Flame top lines:
- attention_kernel_generic 34.7%
- kv_cache_apply 18.2%
- json_validator_sync 12.8%
- tokenization 8.5%
- batch_shard_sync 6.1%
```
Sam (bench): json_validator_sync at 12.8% is suspicious — we validate the whole JSON before streaming? that blocks token streaming path.
Raj (perf): right. validator sync + retries can inflate latency a lot. logs show: `validator: invalid-json, client_retry=1` on ~2.1% of requests -> those triggers extra roundtrips.
Kai (infra): Also note batch formation: json mode tends to produce more variable response lengths so dynamic batching window sometimes flushes earlier -> smaller effective batch sizes. check `effective_batch_size` from traces.
Anya (eng-runtime): I captured a single-request trace where kernel auto picked `atten_generic` vs the text-run which picked `atten_fused_fast`. switching kernel_override to `atten_fused_fast` on json-run reduced p95 to 152ms (so ~13ms improvement).
Sam (bench): good data. but we need apples-to-apples: same kernel, same batching policy, same warmup, same kv cache state. can we do a 2x A/B: text vs json with kernel=forced, batching=constant(16), batch-window-ms=25, kv_cache=off then kv_cache=on?
Raj (perf): agree. action: disable validator for the first A/B to isolate serialization overhead. then re-enable validator and measure validation cost and retry rate.
PerfBot: queued new controlled runs: ab_test_1769877000 (json vs text, kernel=atten_fused_fast, batch_size=16, kv_cache=off), ab_test_1769877300 (same but kv_cache=on)
Anya (eng-runtime): also noticed replay harness vs synthetic traffic difference: replay preserves client-side jitter which created many small bursty windows -> reduces batching. synthetic uniform qps hides that. need to augment synthetic harness to replicate burstiness (burst dist = pareto 1.8, burst_size mean=12).
Sam (bench): +1. I'll patch bench_replay to export per-request timing histogram and to optionally replay exact inter-arrival times. also add a `--strip-metadata` flag that replays prompts with metadata removed to check pure JSON serialization overhead.
Kai (infra): KV cache note: current hashing uses full serialized prompt. structured function-calls inject ordering/noise. propose canonical serialization (sorted keys + compact whitespace) before hashing to improve cache hit rate. that should be low-risk.
Raj (perf): micro-optimizations: move JSON validation off the hot path (validate in async worker or on the consumer side). if we must validate synchronously, prefer a streaming validator that runs as tokens arrive rather than a monolithic parse.
Anya (eng-runtime): we also saw validation failures tied to function arg schemas — validator rejects then client retries with fallback textual output -> that logic causes cascades. we should ensure fallback is not automatic retry but controlled degrade path.
Sam (bench): plan of experiments (short):
- Step A: forced kernel (atten_fused_fast), batch=16 const, kv_cache=off, validator=off, replay exact timings -> measure p50/p95 and effective_batch_size
- Step B: same but validator=on (sync) -> isolate validation cost
- Step C: kv_cache on with canonical serialization -> measure cache hit rate delta
- Step D: run with real-world replay timing + synthetic-burst mode to capture batching sensitivity
- Step E: function-calling heavy sample where metadata present; test async validation + no-auto-retry fallback
I'll own Step A/B/C. Anya/Kai take D/E?
Anya (eng-runtime): I can take D/E, will also produce a small prompt set that strips metadata and one that keeps it so we can compare cache hits.
Raj (perf): once we have A/B/C results, we'll do a kernel ABI-level check to make sure we didn't accidentally fall back to a slower kernel because of sequence length quantization or memory layout.
Kai (infra): I'll add a `trace_id` to each replayed request so we can correlate kernel selection, kv cache hit, and validation outcome in the console traces.
Anya (eng-runtime): sweet. expected timeline: I'll have D/E instrumentation + sample prompts by EOD. Sam/Raj, how long for A/B/C runs?
Sam (bench): runs queued, should finish within 2 hours. will post PerfBot summaries.
Raj (perf): if we still see delta after canonical serialization + async validate + forced kernel + equivalent batching, then it's probably unavoidable serialization CPU overhead. we can consider offloading serialization to a pre-compiled path or native serializer.
Anya (eng-runtime): agree. thanks all. next post will include perfbot links and a short write-up for run methodology so we can keep these apples-to-apples in future. :+1:
Kai (infra): :thumbsup:
PerfBot: run results will be posted to the thread when complete.
